gaps.description: The doc has no bitwise operators; rule 4 reserves symbols for arithmetic and comparison and `and`/`or` are logic words. Invented `shifted right by`, `shifted left by`, `bitand`, `bitor`.

gaps.construct: x << 8 on uint64 discards bits shifted out
gaps.description: Scribe arithmetic is checked; there is no way to request modular / wrapping behaviour. Invented a `wrapping` suffix.
Only Int and Nat appear; no fixed-width integer types. Invented `UInt64`.
Only decimal literals are shown; masks were written in decimal, which hides the bit pattern a reviewer needs to see.
The doc never shows a top-level constant declaration; top-level `let` was assumed.

gaps.construct: Precedence of the invented bit operators
gaps.description: The six precedence levels are not listed, so every bit expression was fully parenthesised.

gaps.construct: Reassigning the parameter x in sequence
gaps.description: No rebinding of parameters; each step gets a fresh let name (harmless, arguably clearer).

doc_rules_contradicted: "Words replace symbols wherever the word is no less clear. Symbols stay only for arithmetic and grouping." - in bit-twiddling code the word forms are markedly less clear than & | << >>, so the rule pushes toward the worse spelling
notes: Bit manipulation is a whole missing sublanguage: fixed-width types, wrapping arithmetic, hex/binary literals and bitwise operators all need first-class forms. The words-over-symbols rule makes these lines roughly twice as long and harder to check against the well-known algorithm.
